div.head:
536. Robert Southey to Mary Barker, 8 July [1800]Address: To/Miss Barker [Bath]
MS: MS untraced; text is taken from Robert Galloway Kirkpatrick Jnr, ‘The Letters of Robert Southey to Mary Barker From 1800 to 1826’ (unpublished PhD, Harvard, 1967), pp. 1–2
Previously published: H. Spencer Scott, ‘Some Southey Letters’, Atlantic Monthly, 89 (1902), 36 [in part].
div.p: I write a few lines by you. so few that only the opportunity of a private hand could excuse them.

You will find at Congreve a copy of Joan of ArcSouthey had sent a copy of Joan of Arc (1798) to Mary Barker’s home at Congreve, Staffordshire. which will arrive as soon as you can do. It will be an earlier remembrancer than the Packet could bring you. &, when you see Thalaba, it will serve like a bad drawing – to show improvement.The Islamic romance Thalaba the Destroyer (1801). I am not however ashamed of it.

If you go thro Plymouth & the fleet be there I have a brother on board the Bellona who will show you what is to be seen. Lieutenant Thomas Southey: he is better than the breed of Sailors in general. only send to him in my name, & he will have brains enough in two minutes to see that you are not a mere Lisbon acquaintance.
God bless you. I love Cintra dearly – but I would rather the rockThe Sierra, or mountain of Cintra. went to England than you.

postscript.p: Do not fail – or delay – to inform us of your arrival. I will watch all the seeding flowers – & send you my Wall & the Cork TreeMary Barker was an amateur painter and may have been teaching Southey to paint. in most accurate painting.
[The first letter I ever received from dear Southey MSlade
nee Barker]The first … Barker: Marginal annotation in hand of Mary Barker; as Mary Barker signs herself ‘Slade’, this was written after her marriage in 1830.
